sourceLineage.origin: Southern Company newsroom — Ratepayer Protection Pledge

observations: Q2 reported earnings were $1.174B/$1.03 per share and adjusted earnings $1.289B/$1.13 while operating revenue was $6.98B, only 0.1% above Q2 2025.

Southern says new energy-intensive customers are structured to bear infrastructure/service costs; the cited OpenAI Georgia project includes financial assurances and up to 1,000 MW flexible demand response.
factors: regulated utility investment and customer growth
large-load AI demand can support durable rate-base growth when customer-specific cost allocation is enforceable
flexible-load agreements can improve grid utilization
risks: earnings growth materially outpaced revenue growth, requiring careful decomposition by Alpha
large-load infrastructure is capital intensive and regulatory/customer-affordability sensitive
contradictions: Strong earnings growth and load-growth narrative coexist with nearly flat reported quarterly revenue; demand should not be inferred from revenue alone.
unknowns: share of forward large-load growth contractually committed versus prospective
project-specific capex, allowed returns and downside protections for large-load customers

recommendation.reason: Primary lineage remains defensible and separates reported execution from prospective large-load economics; Alpha owns numeric underwriting.
